# splunkctl inputs

Manage data inputs.

## inputs create

Create a new data input.

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
splunkctl inputs create [OPTIONS]
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--name` | text | - | Input name/path. [required] |
| `--kind` | choice: monitor, tcp, udp, script, http | - | Input kind. [required] |
| `--index` | text | - | Target index. |
| `--sourcetype` | text | - | Source type. |
| `--disabled` | flag | false | Create disabled. |

## inputs delete

Delete a data input.

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
splunkctl inputs delete [OPTIONS] NAME
```

## inputs disable

Disable an input.

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
splunkctl inputs disable [OPTIONS] NAME
```

## inputs enable

Enable a disabled input.

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
splunkctl inputs enable [OPTIONS] NAME
```

## inputs get

Show details for a specific input.

```text
splunkctl inputs get [OPTIONS] NAME
```

## inputs list

List data inputs.

```text
splunkctl inputs list [OPTIONS]
```

```text
--filter/--limit/--offset apply client-side, after the --kind filter
(the SDK inputs collection is a union across input kinds). Note: the union
collection pages each kind with a 30-per-kind default limit, so environments
with >30 inputs of a single kind may return incomplete results. To verify
completeness for a specific kind, use: splunkctl search oneshot
'| rest /services/data/inputs/<kind>' --limit 10000 (e.g.,
/services/data/inputs/monitor).
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--kind` | choice: monitor, tcp, udp, script, http | - | Filter by input kind. |
| `--limit` | integer range | - | Return at most N entries (default: all). |
| `--offset` | integer range | 0 | Skip the first N entries. |
| `--filter` | text | - | Case-insensitive name substring; --limit/--offset then apply to the filtered set. |

## inputs update

Update an existing data input.

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
splunkctl inputs update [OPTIONS] NAME
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--index` | text | - | Target index. |
| `--sourcetype` | text | - | Source type. |
| `--enabled / --disabled` | flag | - | Enable or disable. |
